items.corrected_text: The city council decided on 10 December 2025 to amend the city's parking-fee ordinance (Parkgebuehrenverordnung 1990) so that the parking fee is 1.10 euro per half hour, effective 1 January 2026. The notice also deletes the last sentence of a paragraph on how the fee is paid and drops annex 10, a template for a short-term-zone vignette.

items.corrected_text: A local news report says the city was running a pilot to give navigation-app providers live occupancy data for 13 larger garages and car parks so that summer visitors are steered to park-and-ride sites. It adds that digital road signs showing occupancy on motorways and main access routes were still to come.

items.corrected_text: A derStandard report says Handyparken had already been replaced by EasyPark in Vorarlberg, Salzburg and Burgenland, and that the other states except Vienna would follow on 1 October, leaving Vienna as the exception. The page itself shows no publication date.

items.note: Page read (published 22 Mar 2023). The 5 EUR summer ticket (July/August at the Messezentrum) is only planned ('soll es dort ... geben'). Draft title '15 Euro fuer ganzen Tag' is a teaser; the site is named 'Nord'/Messezentrum, the text's 'exhibition-centre site' is fine.
items.corrected_text: The city and Salzburg AG agreed a uniform price of 15 euro per day, including public transport tickets for up to five people, at the park-and-ride sites Salzburg Sued and Messezentrum, with a 5 euro all-day ticket planned for July and August at the Messezentrum. A Green councillor said uptake of the sites had stagnated at a low level for years.
items.corrected_title: "P+R" in der Stadt Salzburg wird billiger

items.note: Page read (published 29 Apr 2026). Content matches (three stages to 2036, 1.30 EUR from first phase to 2028 on a per-half-hour basis against today's 1.10, Altstadt tariff zone 2029-2032, plate-based payment machines, scan vehicles; criticism from businesses, OeVP, FPOe). But the page says the city 'plant'/'angedacht' these measures and invites readers to vote; it does not say the city 'presented' it or that it is 'under discussion' in a formal sense, and it is not in force. Keep proposal wording. Title in draft is the og:title; on-page H1 is 'Hoehere Gebuehren und Scan-Autos: Wie denkt ihr ueber die Park-Plaene der Stadt Salzburg?'.
items.corrected_text: A local news report says the city is planning a new parking concept in three stages to 2036, as part of its Mobilitaetsplan 2040: more short-term parking zones and a fee of 1.30 euro per half hour in the first phase to 2028, a special Altstadt tariff zone in 2029-2032, and plate-based payment with camera scan vehicles. These are plans, not measures in force, and local businesses, the OeVP and the FPOe have criticised them.

items.note: Page read (published 21 Jul 2026). The consultation had not yet 'opened': on 19 Feb 2026 the city presented the plan for citizen participation; four in-person events 3-12 March and an online platform from 1 March; participation closes with a Mobilitaetstag on 17 Sept 2026. The 37% -> 20% target refers to motorised individual transport share ('Anteil des motorisierten Individualverkehrs', modal split), by 2040; 'ab 2027 soll die schrittweise, verbindliche Umsetzung ... starten' is correct. Title matches the page title; H1 reads '... So koennt ihr euch einbringen'.
items.corrected_text: On 19 February 2026 the city presented its plan for public participation in the Mobilitaetsplan 2040, with events from March and an online platform from 1 March. The plan aims to cut the share of motorised private transport from about 37 percent to 20 percent by 2040, with step-by-step implementation of measures due to start from 2027.

items.note: Page read (published 21 Jul 2026; real headline is the page title below, H1 is 'Aller Kritik zum Trotz: Umstrittene Salzburger Innenstadt-Sperre bleibt uns erhalten'). Supported and correctly framed as the city's own statements: from 1 July driving bans on central axes along the Salzach, mainly residents, regional commuters and hotel guests (plates S, SL, HA and some Bavarian) may enter; mayor Auinger says traffic flowed smoother than feared; P+R: Salzburg-Sued over 50% more ticket sales vs prior year, Designer Outlet over 117% more; final evaluation planned for year end. NOT on the page: the ADAC coverage and the 7.50 euro P+R ticket. Also the figures are ticket sales vs the previous year, not 'use' generally.
items.corrected_text: The city said on 21 July 2026, three weeks into the summer restriction that started on 1 July, that traffic on the central routes along the Salzach had flowed more smoothly than feared; mainly residents, regional commuters and hotel guests may drive in. The city reported park-and-ride ticket sales up more than 50 percent on the previous year at Salzburg Sued and more than 117 percent at the Designer Outlet, and a final evaluation is planned for the end of the year.
items.corrected_title: Aller Kritik zum Trotz: Salzburger Innenstadt-Sperre auch in den kommenden Jahren

corrected_summary: Salzburg's city council set the parking fee at 1.10 euro per half hour from 1 January 2026, and a local report says the Altstadtgarage hourly tariff rose from 3.30 to 3.60 euro at the start of 2026. In a June 2022 citizen survey, 84.38 percent of valid votes were against expanding the Moenchsberg garage. The city has proposed a parking concept running to 2036 and, by its own account, saw smoother traffic and higher park-and-ride sales in the first weeks of its summer 2026 restriction, with a final evaluation planned for the end of the year.
